title: Finite Gaussian mixtures have an exact posterior-score missing-information identity and Bhattacharyya bound

missing_information.mixture: Let nu=sum_(i=1)^M p_i nu_i with positive fixed finite M, component densities f_i relative to mu=N(0,I), component scores u_i=grad log f_i, mixture density f=sum_i p_i f_i and posterior weights w_i=p_i f_i/f.
missing_information.score_identity: The mixture score is u=sum_i w_i u_i. Therefore U-I_Omega(nu|mu)=E_nu[sum_i w_i |u_i-u|_Omega^2]=(1/2)sum_(i,j)E_nu[w_i w_j |u_i-u_j|_Omega^2], where U=sum_i p_i I_Omega(nu_i|mu).
missing_information.pairwise_bound: Since f>=2 sqrt(p_i p_j f_i f_j), the exact missing information obeys U-I_Omega(nu|mu)<=(1/2)sum_(i<j)sqrt(p_i p_j) int sqrt(f_i f_j)|u_i-u_j|_Omega^2 dmu.
missing_information.gaussian_formula: For nu_i=N(m_i,S_i), set A_ij=(S_i^(-1)+S_j^(-1))/2, H_ij=A_ij^(-1), h_ij=H_ij(S_i^(-1)m_i+S_j^(-1)m_j)/2, B_ij=S_j^(-1)-S_i^(-1), and b_ij=S_i^(-1)m_i-S_j^(-1)m_j. The pair integral equals BC_ij{Tr[B_ij^T Omega B_ij H_ij]+|B_ij h_ij+b_ij|_Omega^2}, where BC_ij=int sqrt(dnu_i dnu_j) is the Gaussian Bhattacharyya coefficient.
missing_information.energy_identity: Because the quartic potential is linear in the law, Q_N(nu)=sum_i p_i Q_N(nu_i)-(U-I_Omega(nu|mu))/4 for positive amplitudes with constant phase.
missing_information.scope_guard: This is exact for a fixed finite mixture with finite weighted score moments. Small overlap makes mixing gain small; the identity does not make overlap small and does not control a growing number of components, non-Gaussian components, phases, textures or nonstationary laws.
